chunks.title: Deck
chunks.paraphrase: A deck has at least 40 cards and no upper limit, at most three copies per card name, and only one kind of Contract card.

chunks.title: Game setup
chunks.paraphrase: Each player starts with 5 Life cores, 3 Reserve cores plus the Soul Core and a 4-card hand, may set a Contract card aside before shuffling, and may redraw once.

chunks.title: Symbols on a card
chunks.paraphrase: Symbols mostly match the card colour, drive cost reduction and Life damage, and include special God and Ultimate symbols, some God symbols also having a colour.

chunks.title: Core Step
chunks.paraphrase: The turn player moves one core from the Void to their Reserve.

chunks.title: Refresh Step
chunks.paraphrase: Exhausted cards on your Field stand up again and the cores in your Trash go back to your Reserve.

chunks.title: First turn exception
chunks.paraphrase: On the very first turn of the game the starting player skips only the Core Step and the Attack Step.

chunks.title: Deploying a Nexus
chunks.paraphrase: Any number of Nexuses may be deployed for their cost, but no cores are placed on Grandwalker or Grandstone Nexuses when they are deployed.

chunks.title: Moving cores
chunks.paraphrase: In the Main Step cores may be moved freely between the Reserve and Field cards, except onto or off Grandwalker and Grandstone Nexuses, and a card left below its lowest level is depleted.

chunks.title: Paying costs
chunks.paraphrase: Matching Field symbols reduce a cost up to its reduction symbols, reduction is mandatory, six-colour reduction symbols take any colour, and only Reserve or ordinary Field cores pay.

chunks.title: Depletion
chunks.paraphrase: A Spirit or Ultimate without enough cores for its lowest level is depleted, which is not destruction, so destruction triggers do not fire.

chunks.title: Cores and the Soul Core
chunks.paraphrase: The Soul Core acts like a normal core but may only sit in the Reserve, on Field cards or in the Trash.

chunks.title: Declaring a block
chunks.paraphrase: The defender may block with one untapped Spirit or Ultimate, which is exhausted, and block-timing effects then trigger.

chunks.title: Battle resolution
chunks.paraphrase: An unblocked attack takes Life equal to its symbols, while a blocked one compares BP.

chunks.title: Destruction after the BP comparison
chunks.paraphrase: The lower BP is destroyed and equal BP destroys both, with destruction effects resolving before the card reaches the Trash.

chunks.title: What a Brave is
chunks.paraphrase: A Brave can stand alone as a Spirit or combine with a fitting Spirit, adding its BP, symbol and effects to it.

chunks.title: Summoning a Brave and direct combine
chunks.paraphrase: A Brave may be summoned as a Spirit or straight onto a fitting Spirit, and summoning it as a Spirit does not count as a Spirit summon.

chunks.title: Combine and separate
chunks.paraphrase: Combining or separating in the Main Step costs nothing, a Spirit takes one Brave, and a pair that stops meeting the condition separates at once.

chunks.title: When a combined Spirit leaves the Field
chunks.anchor: ■ When a Brave Spirit Leaves the Field
chunks.paraphrase: The Brave either stays as a Spirit by taking cores or leaves together with the Spirit to the same place.

chunks.title: Imagine Brave
chunks.paraphrase: An Imagine Brave combines with one Spirit on each side, and each pair then counts as its own combined Spirit.

chunks.title: Saga Brave
chunks.paraphrase: A Saga Brave may also combine with a matching Grandwalker Nexus, which gains its Nexus-combined effects.

chunks.title: What an Ultimate is
chunks.paraphrase: An Ultimate needs at least level 3 when summoned and its Ultimate symbol only reduces Ultimate reduction symbols.

chunks.title: Ultimates on the Field
chunks.paraphrase: Ultimates are a separate card type that effects naming only Spirits do not touch.

chunks.title: Grandwalker Nexus
chunks.paraphrase: Grandwalker Nexuses ignore effects other than their own or ones aimed at Grandwalkers, their God symbol reduces only God costs, and their cores are placed only by effects.

chunks.title: Contract Grandwalker Nexus
chunks.paraphrase: A Contract Grandwalker Nexus is both a Contract card and a Grandwalker, reaches level 2 from your Count, and has a coloured God symbol.

chunks.title: Burst
chunks.paraphrase: One Burst may be set face down per turn and is activated for free when its condition is met.

chunks.title: The Burst Area and Mirage
chunks.paraphrase: One Burst and one Mirage may share the Burst Area, which is outside the Field, so its symbols do not reduce costs.

chunks.title: Seal
chunks.paraphrase: Seal optionally moves your Soul Core into your Life, and [During Seal] effects work while it stays there.

chunks.title: Contract cards at game start
chunks.anchor: ■ Deckbuilding and Rules at the Start of the Game
chunks.paraphrase: A Contract card may be taken out before shuffling and added to the opening hand, which then draws one card fewer.

chunks.title: Soul State
chunks.paraphrase: A Contract card leaving the Field because of the opponent may stay in Soul State instead, where it holds no cores, its symbols do not reduce costs, and most effects cannot touch it.

chunks.title: Manifest
chunks.paraphrase: Manifest summons from the hand by sending the Soul Core to the Trash and paying one cost with a core from a Grandwalker Nexus.

chunks.title: Token cards
chunks.paraphrase: Token cards are prepared outside the deck and only enter the Field through effects.

chunks.title: Effects that activate together
chunks.paraphrase: Constant effects go before timed ones, the turn player orders effects within a group, and an effect caused by a resolving effect resolves first.

chunks.title: Set aside cards
chunks.paraphrase: Set-aside cards can be used like hand cards but are neither the hand nor the Field.

chunks.title: Count
chunks.paraphrase: Count cores sit outside the Field, come from and return to the Void, and are only touched by Count effects.

chunks.title: Over Count
chunks.paraphrase: An Over Count Spirit gets its bonus BP and [During OC] effects while the Count condition holds, whatever its level.

chunks.title: Heavy Exhaust
chunks.paraphrase: Only effects heavy-exhaust a card, which then counts as exhausted and needs one refresh to become normally exhausted.

chunks.title: FAQ effects Q3: can vs cannot
chunks.paraphrase: A 'cannot' effect beats a 'must' effect, which beats a 'may' or 'do' effect.

chunks.title: FAQ effects Q4: immunity order
chunks.paraphrase: 'Cannot be prevented' beats 'unaffected', which beats 'cannot activate'.

chunks.title: FAQ effects Q5: 'by doing X, do Y'
chunks.paraphrase: The X part must be possible and is only done when the Y part can also be done, and the player may skip the whole effect.

chunks.title: FAQ effects Q6: 'if you do'
chunks.paraphrase: With 'you can do X; if you do, Y', X may be done even when Y can only partly be done.

chunks.title: FAQ effects Q9: once per turn
chunks.paraphrase: Once per turn counts per card, while the same-name version counts for all copies of that name.

chunks.title: FAQ: the Soul Core
chunks.paraphrase: When an effect would send the Soul Core to the Void, a normal core goes instead.

chunks.title: FAQ: BP plus and minus
chunks.paraphrase: BP changes stack on the current level, a Spirit at 0 BP is only destroyed by a card clause checked when applied, and "all opposing" BP effects also hit later summons that turn.

chunks.title: FAQ Braves Q1: no Brave on a Brave
chunks.paraphrase: A Brave cannot combine with a Brave or a Nexus that is being treated as a Spirit.

chunks.title: FAQ Braves Q2: a Brave's summon effect
chunks.paraphrase: A Brave's 'when summoned' effect stays a Brave effect even when it is summoned as a Spirit.

chunks.title: No negative values
chunks.paraphrase: Effects never push a printed number below zero.

chunks.title: Void
chunks.paraphrase: The Void is the public core supply with no limit, and more cores are added from outside the game if it runs out.

chunks.title: One Soul Core
chunks.paraphrase: Each player has one Soul Core, which effects naming cores also affect.

chunks.title: Core Step
chunks.paraphrase: The turn player adds one core from the Void to the Reserve, except on the first player's first turn.

chunks.title: Spirit destruction in battle
chunks.paraphrase: BP comparison destroys the loser and the effects of that destruction trigger at that point.

chunks.title: Super Unleash (True Release)
chunks.paraphrase: A card with this keyword reaches level 2 with only the Soul Core on it.

chunks.title: Soul Magic
chunks.paraphrase: A Soul Magic card can be used by paying its whole cost with just the Soul Core while you control a symbol of its colour.

chunks.title: When Destroyed (by the opponent)
chunks.paraphrase: 'When Destroyed' triggers on destruction, and the 'by the opponent' form only on an opposing effect or BP comparison.
